• **Murlikant Rajaram Petkar** was conferred with the **Arjuna Award (Lifetime)** in **2024** for his legendary contributions and outstanding performance in **Para-Swimming**.
 
• He holds the prestigious distinction of being **India’s first Paralympic Gold Medalist**, achieving this feat at the **1972 Summer Paralympics** held in **Heidelberg, Germany**.
 
• Petkar won the **Gold Medal** in the **50m Freestyle Swimming** event, clocking a then-world record time of **37.33 seconds**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Para-Swimming is correct.***
 
• Initially a **boxer** in the **Indian Army**, he switched to swimming and other para-sports after sustaining permanent disabilities during the **1965 Indo-Pak War**.
 
• His life story and struggles were brought to mainstream cinema through the **2024 biopic** titled **"Chandu Champion"**, starring **Kartik Aaryan** and directed by **Kabir Khan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Military Background:**
 
 
• Petkar served as a **jawan** (soldier) in the **Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers (EME)** of the **Indian Army**.
 
• During the **1965 war against Pakistan**, he sustained multiple **bullet wounds** (specifically **9 bullets**), one of which remained lodged in his spine, leading to paraplegia.
 
 
 
• **Versatility in Sports:**
 
 
• Apart from **Para-Swimming**, he was a versatile athlete who competed in **Javelin Throw**, **Precision Javelin Throw**, and **Slalom**.
 
• In the **1972 Paralympics**, besides his gold in swimming, he also reached the finals in **Javelin** and **Slalom** events.
 
 
 
• **Previous Recognitions:**
 
 
• In **2018**, the **Government of India** honored him with the **Padma Shri**, the country's fourth-highest civilian award, for his pioneering role in Indian para-sports.
 
• He was also employed by **TELCO** (now **Tata Motors**) in **Pune** for many years after his retirement from active sports.

• The awards are presented by the **President of India** at the **Rashtrapati Bhavan**.
 
 
 
• **The 1972 Heidelberg Paralympics:**
 
 
• These were the **4th Paralympic Games**. India finished **24th** in the medals tally out of 42 nations, solely due to Petkar's individual performance.
 
• Petkar's gold remained the only **Paralympic gold** for India for several decades until the **2004 Athens Games**.

questions.question: In July 2025, two high-speed unmanned aerial targets were successfully destroyed using the Akash Prime weapon system in which Union Territory of India?

• The successful engagement of these targets took place in the Union Territory of **Ladakh**, which provides a challenging high-altitude environment for testing advanced missile systems.
 
• **Akash Prime** is an enhanced version of the existing **Akash** missile system, specifically upgraded to provide higher reliability and better performance in mountainous terrains.
 
• The system is equipped with an indigenous **active Radio Frequency (RF) seeker**, which significantly improves the accuracy and hit probability of the missile against targets with low radar cross-sections.
 
• The testing in **Ladakh** validates the system’s operational capability near the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**, where air defense is critical due to geographical complexities.

• The system is manufactured by **Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL)** and **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**, representing a hallmark of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
 
 
• **Union Territory of Ladakh**:
 
 
• **Ladakh** was established as a separate Union Territory on **31st October 2019**, following the enactment of the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
 
• It is strategically located, sharing borders with **Tibet** (China), **Gilgit-Baltistan** (Pakistan-occupied), and the Indian state of **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• The region is known for its extreme cold temperatures and high altitudes, such as the **Khardung La** pass, which exceeds **17,000 feet** in elevation.

• **Operational Readiness**: Testing at altitudes above **15,000 feet** is crucial to ensure that the solid-fuel motors and electronic components of the missile function correctly in low-oxygen and sub-zero temperature environments.
 
• **Strategic Significance**: The deployment of such indigenous systems in **Ladakh** strengthens the Indian Armed Forces' defensive posture against aerial threats, including drones, fighter jets, and cruise missiles.
 
• **International Standing**: India has also begun exporting the **Akash** missile system to friendly foreign nations, such as **Armenia**, showcasing the global competitiveness of Indian defense technology in the **year 2024-25**.

questions.question: Under what theme was the International Day for Biological Diversity celebrated in 2025?

options.text: Harmony with Nature and Sustainable Development
Biodiversity: Food, Water and Health for All

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harmony with Nature and Sustainable Development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Day for Biological Diversity (IDB)** is an annual event celebrated globally on **May 22** to promote conservation and raise awareness about the vital importance of biodiversity.
 
• For the year **2025**, the theme **"Harmony with Nature and Sustainable Development"** has been chosen to emphasize the interconnectedness of human progress and environmental health. ***Hence, the correct answer is Harmony with Nature and Sustainable Development.***
 
• This theme aligns with the broader goals of the **United Nations Decade on Ecosystem Restoration (2021–2030)**, highlighting that sustainable development cannot be achieved without protecting the earth's biological variety.
 
• The **2025** focus encourages nations to integrate **biodiversity-friendly practices** into economic planning and infrastructure projects to ensure that development does not come at the cost of the natural world.
 
• It supports the ongoing implementation of the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF)**, which serves as a strategic roadmap to halt and reverse nature loss by the **year 2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History and Origin:**
 
 
• The **International Day for Biological Diversity** was first established by the **Second Committee of the UN General Assembly** in **late 1993**.
 
• Initially, it was observed on **December 29** to mark the date the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)** came into force.
 
• In **December 2000**, the **UN General Assembly** officially shifted the date to **May 22** to commemorate the adoption of the text of the Convention on **May 22, 1992**, at the **Nairobi Final Act**.
 
 
 
• **The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):**
 
 
• The **CBD** is a legally binding treaty with three main goals: **conservation of biological diversity**, **sustainable use** of its components, and the **fair and equitable sharing** of benefits arising from genetic resources.
 
• It was opened for signature at the **Earth Summit** in **Rio de Janeiro** in **June 1992**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Biodiversity:**
 
 
• Biodiversity includes the variety of **plants, animals, and microorganisms**, as well as the **genetic differences** within species and the variety of **ecosystems** (such as deserts, forests, and wetlands).

questions.question: In May 2025, India attacked which country with a BrahMos missile?

__
 
• In **May 2025**, regional tensions led to an engagement where **India** utilized its advanced **BrahMos** missile system against **Pakistan**. This event highlights the strategic importance of high-speed precision weaponry in modern conflict scenarios. ***Hence, the correct answer is Pakistan.***
 
• The **BrahMos** is a **supersonic cruise missile** that was developed as a joint venture between **India's Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and **Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya (NPOM)**.
 
• This missile system is highly regarded as one of the **fastest cruise missiles in the world**, operating at speeds of **Mach 2.8 to 3.0**, which is nearly three times the speed of sound.
 
• The **BrahMos** operates on the **"Fire and Forget"** principle, meaning it does not require further guidance after launch to hit its designated target with extreme precision.
 
• The missile's name is a combination of two major rivers: the **Brahmaputra** of **India** and the **Moskva** of **Russia**, symbolizing the bilateral cooperation between the **two countries**.

__
 
• **Technical Capabilities and Range:**
 
 
• Initially, the range of the **BrahMos** was capped at **290 km** to comply with the **Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR)** guidelines.
 
• Following **India's** entry into the **MTCR** in **June 2016**, the range has been successfully extended to **450 km** and even **800 km** in newer variants.
 
• The missile can be launched from multiple platforms, including **land-based mobile launchers**, **ships**, **submarines**, and **Su-30 MKI fighter aircraft**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• In **March 2022**, a **BrahMos** missile was accidentally fired from **India** into **Pakistan** due to a technical malfunction during routine maintenance, landing near **Mian Channu**.
 
• The **Indian Air Force (IAF)** conducted a high-level inquiry into the **2022** incident, leading to the termination of three officers for deviating from Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
 
 
 
• **Global Export and Demand:**
 
 
• The **BrahMos** missile has gained international attention, with the **Philippines** becoming the first foreign country to sign a deal worth **$375 million** to acquire the shore-based anti-ship variant in **January 2022**.
 
• Several other nations in **Southeast Asia** and the **Middle East** have expressed interest in the missile system due to its **low radar signature** and high lethal power.

• **Strategic Significance:** The deployment and use of **BrahMos** by **India** serves as a major deterrent, providing the **Indian Armed Forces** with a significant "stand-off" range capability.
 
• **Warhead Capacity:** The missile can carry a conventional warhead weighing between **200 and 300 kilograms**, depending on the launch platform and specific mission requirements.
 
• **Flight Ceiling:** It can fly at altitudes as low as **10 meters** (sea-skimming) to avoid detection or as high as **15 kilometers**.

questions.question: During the June 2025 Monetary Policy Committee meeting, the Reserve Bank of India cut cash reserve ratio (CRR) by how many bps?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, during its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meeting concluded in **June 2025**, announced a strategic decision to cut the **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** by **50 basis points (bps)**.
 
• This reduction of **50 bps** (which is equivalent to **0.50%**) is aimed at augmenting the liquidity available within the banking system to support economic growth and ensure smoother credit flow.
 
• By lowering the **CRR**, the **RBI** effectively reduces the amount of cash that commercial banks are mandated to keep with the central bank, thereby increasing their **lendable resources**.
 
• The move was influenced by the need to maintain an "accommodative" or "neutral" stance depending on the prevailing **inflation** and **GDP growth** dynamics observed in the first quarter of the **financial year 2025-26**.
 
• This **50 bps** cut is expected to release a significant amount of primary liquidity into the financial markets, helping banks manage their **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** more efficiently without increasing the cost of funds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**:
 
 
• It refers to the share of **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** that banks must maintain as a cash balance with the **RBI**.
 
• Crucially, banks do not earn any **interest** on the money kept as **CRR**, making it a powerful tool for the **RBI** to control the **money supply** in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Basis Points (bps)**:
 
 
• In financial terminology, **1 basis point** is equal to **1/100th of 1%** or **0.01%**.
 
• Therefore, a **50 bps** cut represents a **0.50%** reduction, while a **100 bps** cut would represent a full **1%** change.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**:
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member** committee constituted by the **Central Government** under **Section 45ZB** of the amended **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• The committee is chaired by the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India** and is tasked with determining the policy rates required to achieve the **inflation target** (typically **4%** with a band of **+/- 2%**).
 
 
 
• **Impact of CRR Cut**:
 
 
• A lower **CRR** results in a higher **Money Multiplier**, as banks have more capital to lend to consumers and businesses.
 
• This usually leads to a decrease in **lending rates** (like **MCLR** or **EBLR**), making loans for housing, automobiles, and industrial expansion more affordable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**: While **CRR** is kept in cash with the **RBI**, **SLR** is the reserve that banks must maintain in the form of liquid assets like **Gold** or **Government Securities** before they can provide credit.
 
• **Repo Rate**: This is the rate at which the **RBI** lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds. It is the primary signal rate for the economy.
 
• **Liquidity Management**: The **RBI** uses instruments like **Open Market Operations (OMO)**, **CRR**, and the **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)** to manage the volume of money in the **Indian economy**.
 
• **Historical Context**: **CRR** levels have historically fluctuated between **3% and 15%** depending on the economic cycle and the **RBI’s** objective to either suck out excess liquidity (inflation control) or inject liquidity (growth stimulus).
